titleStmt.title: Interview with Russell Mack Baldwin, August 2, 2001
titleStmt.author: Thomas Swope

projectDesc.p: Encoded for the Experiencing War web site for the Veterans History Project.

samplingDecl.p: The recording of the interview with Russell Mack Baldwin was digitized.

editorialDecl.p: This transcription was encoded with minimal changes to the original text in an effort to preserve original content and idiosyncrasies of the person interviewed. Period language and terminology are also retained. Encoding is literal with regard to the transcriptionist's capitalization, punctuation, and spelling. Spelling errors are indicated with [sic]; however, recurring errors in spelling within a single document have been marked the first time and not subsequently.

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: This is the oral history of World War II veteran Russell Mack Baldwin. Mr. Baldwin served in the U.S. Army 551 Heavy Ponton Bridge Battalion in the European Theater. His highest rank was T-5. I'm Tom Swope and this recording was made at Mr. Baldwin's home in Euclid, Ohio, on August 2, 2001. Mr. Baldwin was 84 at the time of this recording. All right. And go ahead and read that. We'll just start with you reading that.

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: Can you tell me any specific memories about when Pearl Harbor was bombed? Do you remember anything about that day?

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: That's okay. I've got plenty of tape.

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: A day or so after D-Day?

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: So how did you get out of that? You said you were held in that bunker for 30 days?

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: How did you know that? Had you seen that sort of thing before?

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: How did you get separated from your unit?

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: Do you have any memories of buddies overseas that you got close to?

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: You were restricted from picking up a gun too?

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: Were there, in fact, people that did take a shot at you, though?

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: I mean, that was that same incident?

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: It may be tough to talk about, but I think it's important, if you'd like to talk about any details of the concentration camps.

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: So that if you had seen it from a distance through binoculars or something, you wouldn't shell that building, right?

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: Yeah, I think those kind of things are important to tell. It's not all --

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: When he got over there, he couldn't take it?
